'''''Schoenus nigricans''''' is a species of [[Cyperaceae|sedge]] known by the common names '''black bog-rush'''<ref name=brc>[http://www.brc.ac.uk/plantatlas/index.php?q=node/2264 ''Schoenus nigricans''.] Online Atlas of the British and Irish Flora. Retrieved 13 June 2017.</ref><ref name=jeps>Tucker, G. C. 2017. [http://ucjeps.berkeley.edu/eflora/eflora_display.php?tid=43586 ''Schoenus nigricans''.] The Jepson eFlora. Retrieved 13 June 2017.</ref> and '''black sedge'''.<ref name=fna>[http://www.efloras.org/florataxon.aspx?flora_id=1&taxon_id=220012195 ''Schoenus nigricans''.] Flora of North America. eFloras.org. Retrieved 13 June 2017.</ref> It is native to Eurasia, parts of Africa, Australia, and southern North America, including Mexico and the southernmost United States. 
==Description==
This perennial plant grows in low, tight clumps 20 to 70 centimeters tall, with threadlike leaves bearing wide, dark brown [[ligule]]s. The [[inflorescence]] is a small, flattened cluster of dark spikelets. The fruit is an [[achene]] coated in a hard, white shell.
==Habitat==
''S. nigricans'' grows in many types of [[wetland]]s and other moist and [[alkali soils|alkaline]] habitat, including [[marsh]]es, springs, seeps, [[peat|peat bogs]], [[Heath (habitat)|heath]], and [[Dry lake|alkali flats]].
